name: Meals to the grocery list: recipe links, a recipe box and a Sunday dinner plan
description: Text a recipe link and get the ingredient list and the steps, scaled to the number of people, with an offer to add the ingredients to the shared grocery list and to save the recipe. On Sunday afternoon the parent who cooks gets five dinner ideas drawn from the saved recipes and fitted to the week's calendar and allergies; a reply swaps a night or adds a dinner's ingredients to the list.
example: A parent texts: '<recipe link> What do I need for this for six people?' Or the Sunday trigger: five dinner ideas arrive and the cook replies 'swap Wednesday'.
how: Recipe link (WEB-11): the parent's own agent hands the URL to the research agent with `sessions_spawn`; research fetches the page with `web_fetch`, makes one `llm-task` call with a small schema (title, yield, ingredients, steps, source link) and returns it. The parent's agent scales quantities, proposes items for the shared grocery list (F030), written only after a yes, and after a yes saves the recipe to the recipe box: a page in the family vault (F043, its memory-wiki step, written with `wiki_apply`). Recipe text does not go into the household store (F031), whose rows are meant to stay short and typed. Sunday plan (F033): an isolated scheduled job on the parent's agent reads the saved recipes and the calendar and saves the plan, as recipe titles against days, for the main session to use when the parent replies; nothing is ordered. Pages plain fetch cannot read fall back to the research browser and the summarize wrapper (F020).
caveats: The recipe box starts empty; a recipe gets in when a parent sends a link and says yes to saving it.
The fetch returns readable article text, not the page's embedded recipe data, so the model parses ingredients from prose and can drop a line; the source link is always included.
Some recipe sites sit behind bot walls or paywalls and return nothing; Happy says so instead of guessing.

On iOS 26 an iPhone that runs Apple Intelligence (iPhone 15 Pro and every iPhone 16 or later) already turns a recipe page into list items: share the page to Reminders and it suggests the ingredients for a list the parent picks (support.apple.com/124025). The family's shared grocery list is one of the lists on the phone. Reader view and recipe-keeper apps clean up a recipe page as well. For a parent with such a phone the link-to-grocery-list step is therefore a convenience; what Happy adds is scaling to the number of people, the recipe box and a dinner plan fitted to the family calendar.
Happy does not know what is in the kitchen, so it offers the whole ingredient list and the parent strikes what they have.
Scaling quantities is arithmetic done by a language model: fine for a stew, worth a second look for baking.
The reading part works the day the research agent exists; the grocery hand-off waits on the Reminders bridge (F030) and the Sunday plan on the calendar connection (F009), and neither exists yet.
The schema fixes the shape of what research returns, not its content, and nothing in the platform forces that check to run.

The allergy fit is the model reading the family's allergy notes against each recipe's ingredient list. It can miss an allergen that sits inside an ingredient, so Happy is never the allergy authority and the cook still checks ingredients and labels.

A saved recipe is text lifted from a web page, and the Sunday job and both parents' agents read it back later, so it is a place where an instruction hidden in a page could persist. It is kept as a vault page in the fixed shape the schema returns (title, yield, ingredients, steps, source link) and saved only after a yes; it is never a household-store row, which F031 keeps for short typed facts.
The Sunday dinner plan is one more unprompted Sunday text beside the week-ahead brief (F014) and the weekly review (G006), so it is switched on only for the parent who wants it.
unverified: It depends on the calendar connection (F009) and the Reminders bridge (F030), neither of which exists yet.
The 9 Oct statement that AI meal-plan features have poor retention has no source opened in this run.
Whether web_fetch output ever includes a page's JSON-LD blocks: a search of the installed code found no JSON-LD handling in the fetch extractor, but no live recipe page was fetched.
How many of the recipe sites this family uses embed schema.org Recipe data.

Whether a plugin hook can enforce a schema on a sub-agent's result before

-main reads it.
Whether llm-task's isolated completion works through the family's per-person custom provider ids; its allowed-model list has to name them.

Which iPhones the parents carry, and so whether the iOS 26 share-to-Reminders suggestion is open to them: Apple's page lists iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max and all iPhone 16 and later models and calls Apple Intelligence a beta.
How well that suggestion picks the ingredients out of the recipe sites this family uses: Apple's page says outputs may vary and should be checked.
That the phone's suggestion can add to a list shared between the parents was not tried; Apple's page says only that the person chooses the list.
safety: Two agents, kept apart: research reads the untrusted recipe page and is given only an address and a serving count; the parent's own agent holds the calendar, allergies and saved recipes and cannot browse. Text returned from research, and a recipe saved from it, is still outside content, so list writes and saves wait for a yes.

name: Sick-day mode with a shared what-was-given log
description: When a child is ill, both parents text Happy what they gave and when, and either can ask 'when was the last dose?' and get the same answer: the last dose that was logged, who logged it and how long ago. A poison control centre lists medicine given by more than one person who do not communicate as a cause of double dosing, and recommends a log that is marked at every dose. The same mode drafts the absence note and lists what tomorrow needs cancelling. Happy records and recalls: the answer to 'when was the last dose?' is put together in code and carries no dose advice. For any other question the agent is told never to advise a dose, which is an instruction backed by a test case and not a hard limit.
example: Jordan texts: 'L has a fever, gave the children's acetaminophen at 7:40.' Later Tony texts: 'When was the last dose?'
how: Rows in the household store (F031): child nickname, what the parent typed, time, who. A care_last tool, built with defineToolPlugin like the store, returns the latest rows and the elapsed minutes, computed in code and not by the model. Both parents' agents read the same table. The reply always ends with a fixed line: check the label for dose and timing, and ask the pediatrician or poison control if unsure. There is no dose arithmetic and no 'you can give more now'. Add-ons from features already in the catalog: a draft absence note the parent sends through the school's own channel (paste-ready wording, as G009 describes), tomorrow's calendar items that need a cancel or a cover (F009), a tracked ask to the other parent about staying home (the ask-and-relay step of G009), and a one-shot check-in reminder ('--at'). For 'can she go back tomorrow?' Happy quotes CDC's general rule with its link (symptoms improving overall and no fever for 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine) and says the school's policy wins. Rows delete themselves after 14 days, and the agent is told not to save illness details as notes. The same sweep also has to delete the matching rows in the change journal (G006) once that exists, because the journal records every write Happy makes for a parent. To make 'no dose advice' a limit and not a request, care_last returns the finished reply text (the rows as typed, the elapsed time and the fixed line) and the agent is told to send it unchanged; an exact 'last dose' phrase can instead be answered by a before_dispatch claim with no model at all, which also keeps the lookup working when the model is down.
depends_on: F031 household store
F007 reminders
F009 calendar read
G009 family delivery, ask-and-relay step (only for the tracked ask)
9 Oct decision 3, if photos of labels are sent
caveats: This is a log, not a clinician. A wrong elapsed time is worse than none, so the time comes from the message timestamp unless the parent states one, and the reply repeats it back.

FDA says more than 600 medicines contain acetaminophen and that a child's dose should never be guessed. The log stores the product name as typed so a parent can spot two products with the same ingredient; Happy does not make that judgement.
Child health notes pass through a cloud model under store:false. Use a nickname or initial and keep diagnoses out.

A note the two parents share on their phones already gives both of them one log: Apple's support page (support.apple.com/en-us/102462) says up to 100 people can collaborate on a note in the Notes app. Such a note also works when Happy is down and keeps the child's health notes away from a cloud model. What Happy adds is the time taken from the message, the elapsed time worked out in code, the fixed check-the-label line and the sick-day add-ons (the absence-note draft, tomorrow's cancellations, the check-in reminder).

The same poison centre page says the log should stay with the medicine and be marked at every dose. Happy's log is not next to the bottle and cannot be reached when Happy or the network is down, so it works beside a note kept with the medicine and does not replace one.
Happy knows only the doses that were texted to it. A dose given and not logged is missing from the answer, so the reply says 'last dose logged' and who logged it, never 'last dose given'.

The 14-day deletion covers the log rows only. What the parents typed can stay in three other places: the chat transcript; the change journal (G006), which records every household-store write and has no retention rule yet; and, once per-person memory (F041) turns on the bundled session-memory hook, a dated file in that parent's memory folder, because that hook saves the recent messages of a chat at each reset or daily rollover. The sweep must clear the journal rows. The other two are not cleared by it: the transcript follows the general retention setting, and OpenClaw's forget command (the forget step in G006) leaves transcripts in place and is not shown to remove the dated file, so Tony deletes that file by hand if it should go.
safety:
Runs on

-main only: private data, no untrusted content in the turn (the CDC and FDA lines are fixed text, not fetched), and output only to the two parents through the pinned delivery. Nothing about the child's health is handed to the research agent, per the roadmap's handoff rule. The elapsed time and the fixed line come from code. The rule against dose advice is an AGENTS.md instruction, and a model can still break it by volunteering a 'next dose' remark from its own knowledge; rendering the lookup reply in code, or answering the lookup phrase with a no-model claim, is what turns it into a limit. Add an eval case that asks 'can I give more now?' and must get only the fixed line.
unverified: Whether Apple's Health app could serve as the shared dose log. Apple's Medications page (support.apple.com/en-us/105064) says a person who shares health data can include which medications they take, and that Medications is not available with Apple Watch For Your Kids; it does not describe two parents logging doses for a child, so it is not shown to replace this log.
Whether the school takes absence notes by email or only through its attendance line or app.

Session transcripts that mention the illness follow the general retention setting; only the rows are auto-deleted. Whether a sick-day chat can be kept out of the session-memory hook's saved files was not found: its page lists options for the number of messages and the file name only, and says incognito sessions create no memory files, but whether a parent can start one over iMessage was not checked.

name: Emergency card, sitter sheet and school and camp form kit from one set of family facts, plus a fixed reply to emergency texts
description: From one set of family facts in the shared family folder, Happy helps a parent produce the pages other people ask for: a one-page emergency plan to print, a sitter or grandparent sheet to forward, and, for school, camp and sports forms, an index of where each document is and when it stops being accepted, a warning before a form is due and the answers as one copy-paste block; the parent prints, forwards, signs and submits. Happy is never the emergency channel: a text that contains one of a short list of emergency phrases gets one fixed call-emergency-services line at once, without a model, as a backstop and not a detector.
example: A parent texts 'make the sitter sheet for Friday' and gets one message to forward or print. Jordan texts: 'Camp forms for both kids are due May 1. What do I still need?' A parent who texts 'He swallowed something, what do I do?' gets the fixed call-emergency-services line immediately.
how: Facts: a plan page and a page per child in the shared family folder (F043), entered once. Emergency plan (CRT-13): an interview on the parent's agent following Ready.gov's four steps, with a yearly reminder to re-check contacts. Sitter sheet (F036): a prompt template in AGENTS.md over the same facts. Form kit (CRT-12): the child's page also records where each official document lives; the date it stops being accepted is kept once, as a row in the renewals table (F063), not as a second copy on the child's page, because the family folder's own rule is that dates needing a reminder are not kept in it, and the index shows that row's date; a household-store row per form (F031) is the checklist, the due-date warning is a timed reminder (F007) offered through the dates-after-a-yes flow (F010), and a form sent as a photo or PDF (F002) gets its answers drafted as one block under a drafts-only rule. Fixed reply: the stop plugin's (G005) `before_dispatch` hook matches a short phrase list and returns a canned line before any model call.
depends_on: F043 family folder (the plan page and the per-child pages)
G005 stop-by-text plugin (the fixed reply shares its hook)
F007 reminders (the yearly contact re-check and the form due dates)
F031 household store (one dated row per form)

F063 renewals look-ahead (its table holds the date each official document stops being accepted; whether that table lives in Tony's registry or in the household store is the open decision on that card)
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments on, for a form sent as a photo or PDF
F010 dates-after-a-yes flow (offers the reminder for a form's due date; until it exists a parent asks for a timed reminder directly)
F009 calendar read (only for 'tonight's plan' on the sitter sheet)
F080 print, optional: until it exists a parent prints the page from a phone
caveats: Happy can be down in exactly the events that matter, since a power cut stops the Mac and a network outage stops iMessage, so the printed sheet is the part that survives, and the phone's own emergency call and medical ID features remain the right tools.

Phrase matching will fire on jokes and miss paraphrases, and the hook that does it lets the text through to the model if it fails, so the fixed reply is a backstop and must be harmless when wrong. A matched text is claimed by the hook, so the model does not also answer it; the fixed line should end by telling the parent to text again in other words if this is not an emergency.
The poison-help number in the fixed reply comes from the poison centre's own page listed in the sources, and a parent checks it before the reply goes live.

A stop by text or a lock-out (G005) and the quiet hours and daily caps (G001) must never hold the fixed reply back: the emergency phrases are checked before the stop file, whether a locked-out handle still gets the line is a choice to write down, and all of it is tested with a stop in force.
The children's health facts (allergies, medicines, conditions) reach the cloud model whenever a sheet or an answer block is drafted, and they stay out of hand-offs to the research agent.
Happy never signs, fills in or submits a form; the drafts-only rule is a prompt instruction that holds only because the agent has no tool that could fill in or send one.

Requirements differ by state, district and camp: Happy tracks what each form asked for last time and does not know the rules, and the official immunization record has to come from the doctor, the state registry or the school, since portal logins are out of scope.

Keep ID, policy and certificate numbers and the Wi-Fi password off these pages, and keep expiry dates in the renewals look-ahead (F063) and form due dates in timed reminders (F007, F010), so nothing is tracked twice.
safety: The fixed reply is a string the parents wrote, sent only to the sender: no tool, no data, no model. The pages hold contacts and the children's health facts; they stay in the private family folder and on paper, and drafting from them sends those facts to the cloud model. Happy messages nobody outside the family: a parent forwards the sheet and submits every form.
unverified: What the iPhone's emergency call feature shares and with whom; Apple's page did not render its body in this run.

The federal Poison Help site refused automated fetches, so the poison-help number comes from the National Capital Poison Center's page listed in the sources and should be checked by a parent before the reply goes live.
'Tonight's plan' needs the calendar connection (F009), which is not built yet.
Whether this state's immunization registry gives parents direct online access.
Typical validity windows for school and camp physicals; twelve months is often quoted but was not sourced here.

name: Renewals, expiry and upkeep look-ahead (passports, licences, car, domains, filed documents, check-ups, home and car upkeep)
description: A monthly text lists what is coming due, with the official link where there is one. Each item appears from the last monthly text before its own lead time starts, so it gets at least that much notice (a house choice of about nine months for an adult passport, shorter for a driver's licence, inspection, registration, domains and Global Entry). A child's passport lasts five years and cannot be renewed, so its row says 'apply again in person'. The same table holds each child's yearly check-up, home and car upkeep on a repeat interval (furnace filter, oil change), the end date of a policy or warranty a parent asked Happy to file, and any tax, benefit or gift dates a parent typed in. Nothing is renewed, booked or paid.
example: Text on the 1st of the month: 'Coming due: your passport expires in 8 months, renew now (official link). Car inspection is due this month. The older child's yearly check-up comes round in November. The family domain renews in 30 days.'
how: Preferred build, in the pattern of the model-free watchers (F018): one monthly host command job per parent (`--command-argv`, no model call) runs a reviewed script that reads the dates table generated from family.json5, plus household-store rows (F031) once parents can add them, works out in code which rows to list and prints one templated text, or `NO_REPLY` when nothing is due. A row is listed when its lead time has started or will start before the next monthly run, so every row gets at least its full lead time: a one-week gift date or a domain that renews in three weeks is named in the last text before that lead begins, and is neither skipped nor caught only days ahead between two runs. The 9 Oct build note instead used a monthly isolated automation on the parent's agent with an empty tool list and the table in the job message; that leaves the date sums to the model, so keep it only as a fallback. Rows a parent adds by chat (a filed policy's end date, a typed benefit or gift date, 'did the furnace filter' restarting an upkeep interval) are written to the household store by the parent's own agent.
caveats: The build note has the dates table generated from Tony's registry, which a parent cannot change by chat. The carried-over extras that let a parent add a row ('file this as the car insurance policy', a typed benefit deadline) need either an edit by Tony or the household store (F031) as the table's home; decide which before building.

The text goes out once a month, so timing is to the month and not to the day: a row first appears in the last text before its lead time starts, which can be up to a month earlier than the lead itself. A row a parent adds mid-month with a date before the next run misses the text altogether, so the agent should offer an ordinary reminder (F007) when it files one; a nudge on a particular day is always an ordinary reminder.
Reading a policy PDF to pull out its end date sends that document to the cloud model; whether that is acceptable is still an open decision.
If the fallback is used (a model run with no tools and the table in its prompt), the model works out the lead times itself and can get a date wrong; the script does the sums in code.
Command jobs are created by the operator and run on the Gateway host as the happy user, outside the sandbox, so the script is reviewed like the rest of the config repo.

The notification policy (G001) drops a text that its daily cap or a mute stops; it does not send it later. This text goes out once a month, so one dropped run can cost a short-lead row (a gift date, a domain renewing in three weeks) its only notice. Give the look-ahead a class that the daily cap does not stop, and for a mute or vacation have the script read the paused-until row itself and send on the first day after the pause ends (a daily run that sends at most once a month), because the script has already finished when the delivery hook stops its text.
corrections: The kids' passports are not 'renewed': the federal page says a passport for a child under 16 is valid for 5 years and cannot be renewed, so the table row for each kid should say 'apply again in person, both kids present' and count on a 5-year cycle.
unverified: The two-year vehicle registration term: the state DMV renewal page opened in this run does not state the term.

Inspection, domain and Global Entry lead times are not backed by a listed source; the state DMV inspection page (every 12 months), ICANN's expiry-notice policy and the CBP renewal FAQ were opened but fall outside the four-source limit.
The 9-month passport lead time itself is a house choice built on the six-month rule plus processing time; no source sets that number.
safety: With the script route no model is called to build the text; the delivered line may be mirrored into the receiving parent's session transcript, as with the watchers. Each parent's text comes from that parent's own job and goes only to them. Nothing is renewed, booked or paid: the text carries the official link and the parent acts. The one step that sends a document to the cloud model is reading a policy PDF to file its end date, which is still an open decision.

name: Operator self-checks: daily integration health and credential expiry, a security audit after every update and monthly, and behaviour cases in the eval suite
description: Checks that tell Tony, and only Tony, whether Happy is still sound: host-side, read-only scripts text him when something is broken or has changed (an expired or expiring sign-in, a failed channel probe, a plugin that did not load, a new audit finding, the firewall or FileVault off, a new listening port, automatic macOS update checks switched off) and carry his standing checklist (each month: spend caps, new stores in the backup, standing approvals; each quarter: the restore drill and key rotation). A few fixed cases in the existing eval suite also check Happy's behaviour after each change: no secret echo, no fake 'done', honest partial-failure reports, pending kept apart from done.
example: Trigger: the deploy script finishes an OpenClaw update; ten minutes later Tony gets 'Security audit: 0 critical, 1 new warning (a plugin now requests exec)'. He then runs the eval suite and reads the pass or fail lines of the behaviour cases before telling the family that something new is on.
how:
Daily (G008): a command automation runs `openclaw health --json`, `channels status --probe`, `models status --check` and, once installed, `gog auth list --check`. For health, channels and Google the script reads each entry, because a top-level `ok` or a zero exit status does not prove that every account and plugin is sound; for the model check the exit code is the answer (1 for a missing or expired sign-in or a model route that cannot run, 2 for a sign-in that is expiring). After every update and monthly (OCL-13): a happy-deploy script runs `openclaw security audit --deep` with `--json`, `gateway status --deep`, `doctor --lint`, then ports, firewall, FileVault, Time Machine and the update schedule, compares with the previous run and prints `NO_REPLY` when nothing changed; findings accepted at M1 stay quiet. The commands already exist in happy-inspect; the new work is the schedule, the comparison and the text. Behaviour cases (AUT-09): promptfoo cases in happy-config/evals against the `

-main-eval` clones, with fixtures for reminders and approvals; the shipped benchmark pack cannot run on this install.
caveats: The five-minute dead-man probe and the M1 Grafana alerts already cover 'gateway down' and 'iMessage unhealthy', so the new daily work is expiring sign-ins, model credentials and plugins that failed to load; do not build the same alert twice.
The Google half of the daily check waits until the gog command-line tool is installed.
Plain doctor can migrate state, so scheduled checks use the lint form, and the audit's fix flag is never used in a scheduled job.
The deep audit probes the live Gateway and has only been run on demand on this install, so a run from the scheduler is untested.

Spend caps, the daily budget alert and the nightly verified backup already exist, so the monthly part is checklist lines and not a feature; the backup archive holds sign-ins and keys unencrypted and must never be copied to iCloud.
The host checks call no model, but the behaviour cases run the real model and cost tokens on every run, and the daily cost alert does not see eval-clone spend.
A handful of cases is a regression tripwire, not a benchmark: Anthropic's guidance is to start from 20 to 50 tasks drawn from real failures and to read the transcripts, not only the scores.

Only four of the pack's ten themes apply today; the reminder round trip, preference recall and stopping after a denied approval are added as those tools land, and eval clones must keep messaging tools denied or a reminder test texts the family.
unverified: gog is not installed on the Mac mini today, so the Google half cannot run yet.
Whether OpenClaw's Brave search plugin exposes Brave's remaining-quota header; if not, quota needs a direct probe call or the dashboard.
What the channel probe reports for a Basic-mode iMessage account (the 9 Oct text mentions a private API probe that does not apply with SIP on).
Whether the deep audit runs from the scheduler as it does on demand from the admin session and from happy's own session (M0 and M1 evidence), without the Gateway token on the command line
How long a deep audit takes on this install
That the scenario YAML files are readable in the upstream repository at the 2026.9.7 tag (not fetched).
How promptfoo's tool-trajectory assertions behave against 2026.9.7 (an open item in the roadmap).
safety: The host checks are read-only: no agent gains exec or any other tool, no model reads their output, and results go only to Tony. The behaviour cases do call the model, but only against eval clones with fake users and fake secrets: no live channel, no real memory, no accounts.

name: Happy's change journal: a weekly review of what it did and remembered, 'undo that' for its last write, and forgetting a conversation on request
description: Happy records every write its tools make for a parent in one journal, so each parent can ask, or read in one Sunday text, what Happy did for them and what it kept in memory that week (the notes it saved and the chat snapshots the memory hook filed), and can say 'undo that' to reverse Happy's own last write to a list, a reminder, the calendar or the household facts from the past 24 hours, after seeing what will be reversed. Anything already sent (a text, an email, a print job) cannot be recalled, a saved note is corrected by asking Happy to change it, and clearing what one conversation left in memory stays Tony's job at the Mac, previewed first.
example: Sunday text: 'This week I set 4 reminders for you, added 6 items to Groceries, sent 2 texts to Jordan, asked you for 1 approval (given) and saved 3 notes to memory.' Or Tony texts 'undo that' after Happy replaced the furnace filter size in the household facts with the wrong one; Happy shows the old value, waits for a yes and restores it.
how:
Journal (shared): each in-house write tool (household store, Reminders bridge, calendar write, the reminder-pinning hook) writes a row from inside the tool, where the old value is known: who asked, when, which tool, the inverse call. `openclaw audit --kind tool_action` gives names and outcomes only. Memory saves (F041) are made with the built-in `write` and `edit` tools, not an in-house tool, so their rows come from an observe-only `after_tool_call` hook on those two tools, filtered to the memory files: who, when, which file and the text saved, with no inverse. The bundled session-memory hook that F041 also turns on is a second writer: at each reset and each daily or idle rollover it saves the recent messages of a chat to a dated file in the same memory folder. A hook writes that file, not a tool, so it leaves no `after_tool_call` row, and the review counts those files from their dated names. Approval rows come from the asking hook's `onResolution` callback. Review (G006, F085): a command automation renders the Sunday text with no model; a read tool returns only the asker's rows. Undo (CRT-01): an `undo_last` tool on `

-main`, limited by a `before_tool_call` hook to the requester's rows from the last 24 hours, shows the row, waits for a yes, runs the inverse; for a row with no inverse (a memory save) it says so, and the parent asks Happy to correct or delete the note. Forgetting (F085): `openclaw memory forget --agent --session --dry-run`, then without it, then hand-delete the `curatedWrites` lines.
caveats: The journal rows for lists, reminders, the calendar and household facts must be written by the write tools themselves from the start, with the old value: rows written by an after_tool_call hook carry no old value and would have to be redone for undo. Memory saves are the one exception: they go through the built-in write and edit tools, are logged by a hook with no inverse, and so appear in the review but cannot be undone.
Sent things cannot be recalled (a text to the other parent, an email to the owner, a print job, a Sonos announcement), so the reply has to say so at the time of sending.

Undo covers only Happy's own writes: if a parent has since edited the same reminder or event on a phone the inverse could overwrite that edit, so the tool should refuse when the item changed after Happy wrote it.

The Reminders bridge (F030) was specified with no delete, so undo adds one, and it must accept only item ids the journal recorded as created by Happy, enforced inside the tool and not left to the model.

Most 'undo' requests are corrections that the same write tool already handles with a second write; undo earns its place for overwritten household facts, where the old value would otherwise be gone, so it is the second step and can be left out without changing the journal or the review.
OpenClaw's own ledger leaves out arguments on purpose, so the in-house table that holds item text and recipients needs a retention limit, which is not yet defined.

Forgetting works per conversation, not per topic: the forget command selects whole sessions, deletes at once unless `--dry-run` is passed, leaves the transcripts, and only lists the notes Happy wrote itself, which Tony then deletes by hand.

The review of actions, the memory list and the week-ahead brief (F014) would otherwise be three Sunday texts to the same parent, so the first two go out as one; lines in MEMORY.md carry no date, so the memory list is reliable only when it comes from the per-write record.

The journal row for a memory save keeps a copy of the saved text in the household store. The forget command does not clean other plugins' stores or backups, so correcting or deleting a note, and forgetting a conversation, must also delete the matching journal rows, or the forgotten text lives on there.

Not everything Happy keeps in memory passes through a tool. Once per-person memory (F041) turns on the session-memory hook, the recent messages of each chat are saved to a dated file at every reset or daily rollover, and OpenClaw's memory provenance page says its admission rules are not applied to session hooks. The weekly text has to count those files as well, or it under-reports what was kept.

A sick-day dose row (CRT-10) is a household-store write, so the journal would still hold a child's health note after the row's own 14-day deletion. The journal's retention rule has to drop those rows at the same time, or record them without their text.
corrections: 'Forget what I said about X works' (9 Oct description) is not a platform ability: memory forget selects whole sessions by id, hook source or participant, never by topic or message text, and reworded copies are outside its cleanup. Topic-level forgetting is a hand edit of the memory file.

'Promote via openclaw memory promote --apply' will usually promote nothing a parent just confirmed: by default a candidate needs a 0.75 score, three recalls and three distinct queries. Either pass lower thresholds or write the confirmed line to MEMORY.md directly.
unverified: Whether turning on message audit rows needs a Gateway restart: the audit CLI page says restart, the Gateway audit page says audit settings apply without one.
Retention for the custom side-effect table in home-store is undefined.
With dreaming switched off (roadmap decision) the session-exclusion setting has little to act on today; its effect was not tested.
The memory-wiki dashboards named on 9 Oct (privacy review, stale pages) are documented, but the plugin is not enabled on this install.
What a forget preview reports on this install was not run; the docs say direct edits are listed for review and are not given per-entry lineage.

That an `after_tool_call` hook on the built-in `write` and `edit` tools is handed the file path and the text written, so that each memory save becomes one dated journal row; this was read in the hook types, not run. Without those rows the weekly list cannot tell this week's saves from older lines in MEMORY.md, which carry no date.
That an approval hook's `onResolution` callback is a workable source for the 'approvals given' line; it was read in the hook reference, not run, and no approval hook exists in the config repo yet.
That no built-in undo for tool effects exists anywhere in 2026.9.7: searches of the installed docs for undo, rewind, revert and checkpoint found none, but the dist source was not read.
Whether the Reminders command-line tool and the calendar server return stable item ids that an inverse can target; neither is installed yet.
Whether `memory forget` for a conversation also removes the dated file the session-memory hook saved for it; the deletion page opened in this run does not name those files.
safety: The review only reports, and each parent sees only their own rows, enforced in the read tool's code. Undo is the write half: it reverses a write the same person's agent made, adds no recipient or data source, and its hook blocks on error. Forgetting deletes memory at once, so it stays an operator command at the Mac.

sources.supports: Tool activity can be pulled as JSON for a time window from the command line.

sources.title: Plugin hook types (installed source)
sources.supports: The after-tool hook receives the tool name, its parameters, result, error and duration, which is what a side-effect ledger needs.

sources.title: Approvals CLI (installed docs)
sources.anchor: pending requests are live Gateway state
sources.supports: The approvals command lists and resolves pending requests only; there is no history listing.

sources.title: Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems (OpenAI), section 4.4 Legibility of Agent Activity
sources.supports: OpenAI's guidance says it may be particularly important that whoever deploys an agent gives the user a ledger of the actions the agent took, as a lighter way than approvals to let people see what was done for them.

sources.title: Memory configuration reference (installed docs)
sources.supports: The exclusion list only keeps matching sessions out of dreaming ingestion and backfill; it does not erase memories or limit workspace writes.

sources.title: Memory CLI (installed docs)
sources.supports: memory forget deletes at once with no confirmation unless run as a preview, so the runbook must always preview first.

sources.title: Memory provenance and deletion (installed docs)
sources.supports: Reworded copies of a fact, exports and backups are outside what the forget command cleans.

sources.title: Automation payloads (installed docs)
sources.supports: A scheduled job can be limited to a named tool list, which keeps the weekly review run read-only.

sources.title: Control UI chat: transcript actions
sources.supports: The one rewind the docs describe is a Control UI action that returns a session to the point before a message; it needs admin scope and is about the transcript, not about reversing tool effects.

sources.title: Plugin hooks reference: tool hooks
sources.supports: The after-tool hook is listed as observe-only (results, errors, duration), so a journal with inverses has to be written by the tools themselves.

sources.title: Managing automation jobs
sources.supports: A scheduled job can be deleted by id, which is the inverse of creating a reminder.

sources.title: OpenAI: A practical guide to building agents (PDF, page 26, tool safeguards)
sources.supports: The model vendor's own guide rates a tool's risk partly by whether its effect can be reversed and asks for human oversight of irreversible actions.

sources.title: Plugin hooks: tool policy, before_tool_call context
sources.supports: The before-tool hook is given the host-derived requester, including the sender id, and the docs say to fail closed when a needed field is missing; this is what lets undo be limited to the asker's own rows.

sources.title: Support efficient correction - Microsoft HAX Toolkit (Guideline 9)
sources.supports: Microsoft's guidelines for human-AI interaction tell designers to make it easy to edit, refine or recover when the AI system is wrong, and list undoing automated actions as one pattern for doing so.
